newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GRISSOM MAKES NO EXCUSES: "I MADE AN ERROR".
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GRISSOM MAKES NO EXCUSES: "I MADE AN ERROR".

text.p: Marquis Grissom had a dozen chances to come up with an excuse for the shocking fielding lapse that helped set up the Atlanta Braves' 1-0 World Series loss Thursday night to the New York Yankees.

But the stalwart centre fielder, awarded his fourth successive Gold Glove award for fielding excellence this season, was determined to tell the truth, and only the truth, in four simple words: "I made an error."
In the top of the fourth, Yankee third baseman Charlie Hayes led off with a high drive deep into right centre.
Grissom and rookie right-fielder Jermaine Dye converged on it. With Dye crossing in front of him, the ball took a shattering bounce off Grissom's glove, allowing Hayes to hustle his way to second.

Two batters later, Yankee first baseman Cecil Fielder lashed a double down the third-base line and Hayes headed home to score the only game's only run in a result that put New York within one more victory of winning the series.

"It's a ball I probably should have caught under the circumstances. But I made an error. Y'all seen it for yourselves," Grissom told reporters who crowded around him in the clubhouse to offer him one opportunity after another to blame the mishap on a miscommunication with Dye.
"It could have been. But I made an error -- bottom line. I made an error and ain't nobody need to make no other excuses about it.
"I made an error, and in the newspaper tomorrow it's going to say Grissom made an error. E-8. E-8," snapped the 29-year-old veteran, referring to the scoring shorthand for error, centre fielder.
Grissom's irritation over repeated attempts to draw him into excuse-making was as clear as the snake tattoo on his right bicep.
Was he talking to Dye as they converged in the outfield?
"You can't hear nothing. With the crowd screaming, you can't hear nothing in that situation. I made an error. So that's the end of that," he said.
But trying to pin the loss of the game on him for his error would be taking the matter too far.
"We've got to score some runs to win anyway. We didn't score no runs. We didn't swing the bat as well as we wanted to," said Grissom, who got two of the defending series champion Braves' five hits.
